subject: Discovery: relevance & re-rank evaluation (recap + AM action items)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Emma Turner <emma@hyperscaleretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap + next steps — relevance & rerank evaluation

Emma — great conversation earlier today, thanks for taking the time. Below is a short recap of what we heard, the success criteria you shared, and the proposed next steps so we can scope a short evaluation. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points
- Search relevance dropping on long-tail SKUs and seasonal catalogs (top complaint from merchandising).
- Current rerank pipeline is expensive at scale (per-query embedding lookups + re-ranker model inference).
- Cold-start latency for new queries and recent SKUs (cache warmup is inconsistent).

Current stack (what you told us)
- Primary product search: ElasticSearch (docs + sparse BM25 ranking) + in-house feature signals.
- Vector store for embeddings: using VectorDB Cloud (hosted) for 30M vectors (currently storing product title + sparse attributes).
- Re-ranker: lightweight Transformer (distilbert) running on CPU autoscaled pods; invoked for top-50 candidates.
- Traffic pattern: heavy read peaks 7–11AM ET; non-uniform distribution with long-tail queries accounting for ~40% of queries.

Index scale & performance targets
- Index size: ~30M active vectors, expected to grow to 70M in 6–9 months.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 220ms end-to-end for search + rerank under normal load; 95th <= 350ms during planned spikes.
- Cost target: reduce per-1000-query inference cost by >=30% vs current baseline.
- Batch patterns: batch re-ranker calls only at archive/bulk jobs; foreground queries should aim for low single-request latency.

Success criteria for a short evaluation (2–3 weeks)
1) Maintain or improve NDCG@10 on your canonical eval set (we discussed a small labeled set of ~2k queries).
2) Meet 95th percentile latency target (<= 220ms) on a production-ish traffic replay.
3) Demonstrate a cost per 1k queries that is <= 70% of your current cost using our recommendations (batching, caching, quantized model).

Proposed next steps (timeline)
- Action A (this week): you share the canonical eval set + a small traffic replay (we can accept redacted IDs). Attachment: sample_prompt_set.csv is an example format.
- Action B (by 6/18): Redwood team (Mateo + Marcus) will provision a dedicated test route and run a dry replay with a candidate reranker + caching profile.
- Action C (by 6/25): run a live A/B with a small percentage of traffic or a production replay and deliver NDCG/latency/cost report.

Attachments: HSR_IRD_v1.pdf (initial question list), sample_prompt_set.csv (example labels).

Open questions we asked you to confirm
- Do you want item embeddings to include price/stock attributes or keep them in sparse features?
- Is the 95th percentile latency target strict across all geographies or only US traffic?

Thanks again — if the above looks right I’ll schedule the technical kickoff with Mateo and Marcus for Friday morning PT.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks Olga — this is an excellent summary and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and notes:

- Confirm: include price and stock as dense features in the embedding vector for now — merchandising believes it improves ranking for promos. We can experiment later.
- Geography: for the pilot, only US traffic matters. We will evaluate EU later when we scale.
- Eval set: attached is the initial CSV with 2,100 labeled queries (redacted product IDs). We'll upload a replay file to the drive link you provided by EOD Friday.

One outstanding: how do you handle cold-starts for brand-new SKUs that have no historical signals? Right now our caches are empty and it kills relevance for new drops. Can the Redwood caching approach be tuned for immediate warm starts?

Also looping in procurement — they may have a short procurement questionnaire once we define test infra.

Regards,
Emma Turner
Senior Product Manager — Search & Discovery
HyperScale Retail

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: internal — notes from HSR discovery

Internal notes / technical flags so we can prep for the kickoff: 

- Vector storage: 30M -> 70M in months implies we should test both IVF+PQ and HNSW config; measure index build time and memory. Recommend starting with PQ quantization to hit cost targets.
- Reranker: current top-50 candidate size is high. Propose testing top-20 + stronger sparse hybrid scoring to reduce re-ranker calls.
- Caching: recommend prefix/KV cache for recently seen SKUs and a small LRU warmup for new SKU bursts. Cold-start: use attribute-based fallback (title + category embedding) to synthesize a seed embedding for new SKU until product signals arrive.
- Replay plan: need a 2–3 hour high-variance slice (7–11AM ET) and a cold-start slice that includes recent SKUs rolled in. Ask Emma to annotate the replay with event timestamps and flags for new product launches.

Requested items before kickoff:
1) Eval set CSV (we asked for 2k, got 2.1k — good)
2) Traffic replay (redacted IDs) with a labeled spike window
3) Confirmation whether VectorDB Cloud currently exposes vector shard topology (we may need sharding hints).

I’ll draft a short runbook for the test infra and attach it to the kickoff invite.

— Mateo
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
